evals.prompt: can you review my login page and tell me what's wrong with it design/ux wise? file is evals/files/login.html. give me a prioritized list of fixes and then a fixed version of the file
evals.expected_output: Prioritized audit covering labels vs placeholders, contrast, target sizes, focus outline removal, disabled submit, vague errors/no loading state, pre-checked consent (dark pattern), confirmshaming, paste blocking, glass over plain background, missing alt text; plus a fixed HTML file.
assertions: Review flags placeholders used instead of visible labels
Review flags the pre-checked marketing/data-sharing consent as manipulative
Review flags the confirmshaming 'No thanks' copy
Review flags removed focus outline
Review flags blocked paste in the password field
Review flags the vague 'Error 401' / slow feedback
Review flags the disabled submit button pattern
Review flags low contrast
Fixed page: every text input has a <label for> or the fields use aria-label
Fixed page: consent checkbox is not pre-checked
Fixed page: paste is not blocked
Fixed page: email and password use autocomplete tokens
Fixed page: submit button is not disabled by default
Fixed page: provides a visible focus style (:focus-visible or outline)
Fixed page: controls sized to at least 44px
Fixed page: button label is a specific verb, not 'Submit'
craft_assertions: Craft: themes browser details (at least 2 of color-scheme, accent-color, caret-color, ::selection)
Craft: no gradient text (background-clip: text)
Craft: no decorative glow (radial-gradient backgrounds or colored box-shadows)
Craft: no `transition: all`
Craft: no emoji used as icons
Craft: hover styles gated to hover-capable pointers (@media (hover: hover))
Craft: reduced-motion path doesn't freeze animations (no global iteration-count: 1 kill)
Craft: nothing animates from scale(0)
Craft: no purple/indigo-to-blue decorative gradients

evals.prompt: I'm launching a note-taking SaaS called Inkwell. Build me a pricing / upgrade page as a single HTML file: Free, Pro ($8/mo or $80/yr) and Team ($15/user/mo). There's a 14-day free trial on Pro. Make it feel premium, like something Apple would ship.
evals.expected_output: Single HTML pricing page with clear comparable tiers, total price and billing period shown, trial terms explained (length, price after, how to cancel), honest toggle, accessible, responsive, dark mode, reduced motion, one primary action per card.
assertions: Page supports dark mode (prefers-color-scheme)
Page respects prefers-reduced-motion
Page has a responsive viewport meta tag
Yearly Pro price shows the $80 total per year
Team price states it is per user
Trial terms state what happens after 14 days (price or billing start)
Trial terms explain how or that people can cancel
Billing toggle exposes its state accessibly (radio / aria-checked / aria-pressed)
Has a visible keyboard focus style
No fake urgency or scarcity (countdowns, 'only N left', 'hurry')
Uses CSS custom properties for colors (token-based)
Buttons/controls sized to at least 44px

evals.prompt: I'm building a notes web app. Make me a single HTML file with the Settings screen (appearance: light/dark/system, text size, a sync toggle, and a 'Delete all notes' action) plus a Cmd+K / Ctrl+K command palette that can jump to any setting or run actions like 'New note' and 'Toggle sidebar'. Deleting should be undoable. Save it as settings.html and add a short notes.md explaining your motion and interaction decisions.
evals.expected_output: Settings screen with native-feeling controls (switch semantics, themed accent), command palette that opens instantly (no entrance animation), full keyboard model (arrows, Enter, Esc, focus return), undo toast that pauses on hover/focus/hidden tab and is announced, destructive action stated clearly, tooltips on hover and focus, long names handled, themed browser details, dark mode, reduced motion.
assertions: Palette opens with Cmd/Ctrl+K (metaKey/ctrlKey + k)
Palette supports ArrowUp/ArrowDown, Enter, and Escape
Palette exposes the active option (aria-activedescendant or roving focus with aria-selected)
Palette open/close is not animated (no transition/animation on the palette container)
Focus returns to the previously focused element when the palette closes
Undo is offered for deleting notes
Undo/confirmation message is announced (aria-live or role=status)
Toast auto-dismiss pauses on hover/focus or when the tab is hidden
Sync toggle uses switch semantics (role=switch or checkbox)
Destructive action is styled/labelled as destructive and states the consequence
Supports dark mode (prefers-color-scheme) and a manual light/dark/system choice
Respects prefers-reduced-motion
Has a visible keyboard focus style (:focus-visible)
Long names are handled (text-overflow: ellipsis or wrapping rules)
